$comment: Checks this repository asks harnessimo to enforce. The proof-marker and track rules were written here first and moved into the package; locked surfaces and cold start are what this repository gains in return. src/platform/docs-proof.ts keeps the project-specific parts and delegates the rules.

coldStart.$comment: The commands `task typecheck` runs, spelled out rather than invoked through Task: a newcomer with a fresh clone has pnpm and Node, and requiring a separate binary before anything can be verified is exactly what the cold-start test exists to catch. Typegen comes first because Next.js generates route types into .next/types, so a bare tsc fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The full `task check` additionally needs Deno and a Playwright browser; a cold start that fails for a missing runner measures the runner.

cleanExit.$comment: Lecture 12. Scoped to what a session changed. console.log is a marker here because this is an application and its logging goes through the structured logger with a correlation_id — but scripts/ is exempt, since those are command-line tools whose output is the product. The progress rule is off on purpose: in this repository 'where I stopped' lives in the handoff of whichever track was worked (HDD), and which handoff that should have been is not machine-decidable; specs/TRACKS.md is an index of live tracks, not a session log.

instructions.$comment: AGENTS.md is the router every agent tool loads first; DEBT.md is a register, not an instruction file, and is deliberately not limited.

boundaries.$comment: Two invariants from AGENTS.md that were prose until harnessimo 0.10 could say them. Both held on the day they were switched on; the point is that they keep holding without anyone remembering to look.

rules.reason:
the service-role key bypasses RLS, so a client-side use is a data leak wearing an ordinary import
      fix:  reach it through src/platform/supabase/service-client.ts from a route handler, never from a component

design tokens live in one file, so a hard-coded colour is a theme that stops being one
      fix:  add the token to src/app/globals.css and use it
